Subject: Dedicated capacity ask for Q4 launch — preliminary numbers attached

Hi Dylan / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Mnemosyne is moving fast on the inference side and we want to lock in dedicated capacity for our Q4 public beta. High level ask: 48 reserved GPUs (A100-equivalent) starting 2027-10-01 with a phased ramp (16 / 32 / 48 over three weeks) and a short-term burst lane for launch weekend. Our procurement team needs an estimated monthly commitment and an expected SLA for tail latency.

Attached is the RFP excerpt that lists peak QPS and model sizes. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to a calendar-roll start on 2027-10-01 and what the likely allocation window is if there are competing deals? We are sensitive to price but will pay a launch premium if we get strict isolation for the first 30 days.

[attachment: Mnemosyne_RFP_Q3.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)]

Team — technical feasibility and tradeoffs below. Short version: we can accommodate Mnemosyne, but only with compromises or temporary measures unless another committed start is moved. Options and approximate impact:

1) Staggered reserved ramp (recommended): 16 GPUs on 10/01, +16 on 10/08, +16 on 10/15. Minimal infra changes; acceptable tail latency SLA with reserved pools.

2) Partial isolation + multi-tenant quantized variant: 32 isolated GPUs + 16 on multi-tenant quantized fleet. Reduces cost but may increase tail latency 15–30ms under peak.

3) Temporary burst lane (best-effort): provide a preemptible burst of up to 12 GPUs for launch weekend only. This requires a fallback policy and clear SLAs for eviction.

4) Move internal PoC (low business value) — frees up 20 GPUs for early start. Requires leadership approval; not ideal but possible.

I’m attaching a quick tradeoff table showing cost delta, expected latency change, and infra effort. If business wants strict isolation on 10/01, we need a signed commitment and confirmation that we can shift lower-priority starts (option 4). Otherwise option 1 with a guaranteed ramp is the safest.

[attachment: qv_tradeoff_table.csv (csv, 12KB)]

—Kar
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Infra Eng, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Raj — thanks for the fast turnaround. Summary and proposal based on infra and ops input:

Proposal (opt-in):
- Staggered ramp to 48 GPUs: 16 on 2027-10-01, +16 on 2027-10-08, +16 on 2027-10-15 (option 1).
- Reserved pools guaranteed for each stage with an SLA for tail latency; we will offer a documented 30-day launch premium option to convert the entire pool to strict isolation for the first 30 days at an additional monthly cost (we will share pricing via Vanessa).
- One-time best-effort burst lane of up to 12 GPUs for launch weekend subject to eviction policies. Will include a fallback to the quantized multi-tenant variant if eviction occurs.

Action items and asks:
- Raj/Contracts: confirm acceptance of the staggered ramp + whether you want the 30-day isolation premium. If yes, we’ll issue a draft SOW reflecting MNEM-2027-0719 and a DocuSign link.
- Vanessa: please follow up with pricing and a MAP by EOD tomorrow.
- Kar: begin scheduling the staging and any config changes for quantized variants; we’ll target a dry-run with Mnemosyne two weeks before 10/01.

If Mnemosyne needs strict isolation on 10/01 and is willing to pay the premium AND sign by 2027-09-08, we will explore re-prioritizing the internal PoC; otherwise the staggered plan is our operationally safe window.

Raj — happy to hop on a call at 4pm PT today if you want to lock details.

—Dylan
